subject: Model average of multisession and density with habitat covariates

messages.author: a1ea1e6532b5c795
messages.subject: Model average of multisession and density with habitat covariates
parts:
HI all

I am seeking some advice. We have several camera trap surveys of two months each, from which we identified different carnivore species and these were set at different regions of a protected area, over a period of 6 years

Here is a summary of the data for one of the species:
                   data2 data3 data4 data5 
Occasions        95      468      659     1554    
Detections      151       88       53       82    
Animals          58       32       23       25    
Detectors        81       41       51       78    

 data2 data3 data4 data5  
 "F"      "F"      "F"      "F"          
 "M"      "M"      "M"      "M"            

After being able to model each survey/year independently as the data came in, we now want to calculate densities of each species over the whole park (the mask is the park with added habitat covariates), by using a multi-session approach (year = session) and letting density vary by session and g0 and sigma vary by sex. 
Will the model average over the multi-session outputs give the intended overall density result? Will we be able to predictDsurface on the average model? We are able to obtain for each session reliable estimates with the following model structure:
lapply(data,secr.fit, model=list(D~Session,g0~h2,sigma~h2),mask=MASK, hcov="Sex",trace = FALSE,method = 'Nelder-Mead')

But we keep failing when we start to add the habitat covariates (Vegetation, Water...) to the density model and we keep getting the Error: vector memory exhausted (limit reached?)

Any insight is most welcomed, thank you

Rafael

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Model average of multisession and density with habitat covariates, or what you are trying to do.
parts:
Rafael
I can't quite follow how your surveys relate to years and sessions.
1. Can we assume you are analysing species separately?
2. I take it you don't want to model temporal variation, rather to assume no temporal variation and focus on space?
3. Something must be wrong for you to have 1554 occasions in two months.
4. Are you really interested in averaging over models (which models?)? Or just getting an average density across years and covariates?
5. I haven't thought about model-averaging the predicted density surface - it's possible in principle, but you might have to compute it yourself.
6. I can't see where the memory problem comes from. Although you attribute it to including habitat covariates of density, that may merely be the straw that broke the camel's back. It's not surprising you run out of memory if the number of occasions is artficially inflated. Also, you can fit models using a mask that discards pixels distant from any detector, and later extrapolate that model to a much larger mask for the whole park.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Model average of multisession and density with habitat covariates, or what you are trying to do.
parts:
That helps. If I'm understanding your design right, it seems time and space are confounded - you might argue that one or the other is unimportant, but I don't think you can have both without a more rigorous (randomized) design.
If each survey is a 'session' in 'secr' then you can model the session differences with a session covariate (possibly grouping similar times or habitats). (If the covariate is a factor then it can be coded with a mean effect as described in a different context here section 7.8). If you go the other route of fitting spatial covariates of density then, yes, I think you can use predictDsurface, but the details will depend on your model.

On (6) I meant 'can' i.e. you can fit a model efficiently with a restricted mask and extrapolate later with a larger mask.
Murray
